newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lankan president sees early end to ethnic war.
newsitem.headline: S.Lankan president sees early end to ethnic war.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga said on Friday she saw an early end to the country's bloody ethnic war but added that a durable solution would have to be political.

Addressing passing-out parade of army officers in Colombo, Kumaratunga said she would need the military's help to defeat the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels who she claimed were incapable of talking peace.
"If we have to defeat them, we will do so," she said.

"(But) the military campaign will only facilitate a situation so that we can impose peace in our country. We might have to impose it, unfortunately even for those small ruthless and murderous groups," she said.

"Once the military conflict is over, very soon I hope if all goes well, the security forces can be used in other fields of development, human creation and building prosperity in our country," Kumaratunga said.
Kumaratunga's People's Alliance was elected into office in 1994 on a platform of ending the ethnic war and bringing peace to the Indian Ocean island.
The government is bringing in a new constitution as part of its peace package that is aimed at devolving more powers to minorities.
"It is a complicated, difficult and daunting task, but we will do it," Kumaratunga told the new officers.

The LTTE have been fighting since 1983 for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, but the LTTE put the toll higher.
